viewer_sees: A man covered head to foot in gold dust stands on a reed raft in the exact middle of a round mountain lake at dawn, incense smoke rising, the whole shore ringed by steep green walls and not one building
An old chronicler writes by candlelight in a whitewashed study in colonial Bogota, the quill moving across a thick page
An old Muisca lord sits at a low fire in a highland yard and tells his story toward an empty stool at the right where the chronicler sat
The young heir sits small and thin deep inside a cave mouth at dawn, a thin thread of cave fire, the highland outside pale and cold
LOCKED VIEW out of the cave mouth over six years: the heir sits at the left on a reed mat beside one plain bowl, and the weather outside the opening turns through dry gold, rain, mist and frost
The heir steps out of the cave at night to look at the moon and the stars; as the camera rises, a far lake glints silver in the dark bowl below
Muisca builders lash a great raft of reeds at the shore and set four clay braziers on it; incense smoke thickens until it dims the daylight
Crowds in feathers and gold crowns pack the whole shore ring around the lake, small bright figures against green slopes
Attendants smear the heir with sticky earth and dust him with powdered gold at the water edge until he glitters from head to foot
The gold-covered heir stands on the raft with a heap of gold and emeralds at his feet and exactly four chiefs beside him, braziers smoking at the corners
Horns sound and the shore roars as the raft is poled out toward the middle of the lake
A flag goes up for silence; the heir flings his gold into the water in one arc, and the four chiefs throw theirs
The flag comes down and the shore erupts again; the gilded heir stands alone at the center of the raft, lord of the lake
Under the water, gold figurines, discs and emeralds sink slowly through dark green water, glinting once each as they fall: a gift, not a hoard
A highland market where Muisca traders swap salt cakes and cotton mantles for gold; the camera slides right along the trail to a stream where a gold figurine is lowered into the water
In Quito, a Muisca man from the Bogota country tells a circle of Spanish soldiers about the gilded lord, hands sketching a man covered in gold
Belalcazar in steel helmet and breastplate rises from the fire and points up the mountains, calling for the gilded man
Three mounted Spanish captains crest a ridge; the camera pushes past them over a misty plateau of thatched round houses and a lake: gold and emeralds on a cloth, but no golden city
A hand-drawn 17th century European map of the Guiana lands: a tiny gilded man icon becomes a golden town, then a huge inland lake called Parime, sea monsters and compass rose in the margins
Raleigh stands at the rail of an Elizabethan ship moving up a jungle river, looking upstream toward a bend that never ends
EMPTY AFTERMATH: a rusted morion helmet, a broken iron-bound chest, a torn banner and a snapped spade half sunk in jungle mud on a shore, the camera drifting to a still silent lake
Laborers cut a V-shaped notch through the rim of the lake and the water pours out through the channel, exposing a gleaming mud shore while Sepulveda in a wide hat directs them
The second, deeper cut slumps and the water creeps back; the camera pans right along the muddy rim to a plain grave where Freyle and two workers fill in the earth over a poor man
A Pasca farmer in a felt hat and ruana kneels in a cave in 1969, lifts the lid of a clay jar and finds gold and pottery gleaming in his torchlight
The small gold raft: a seated chief at the center, ten smaller figures standing around him, some masked, the surface granular as if it all came from one pour
PROCESS CUTAWAY: a clay casting mold cut open to show the charcoal core and molten gold flowing in to fill ten tiny figures and one seated chief in a single pour
A relief map of the Andean highlands: a gold dot at Pasca far from a ringed round lake at Guatavita, a thin dotted line drawing itself between them
A ghost of a reed raft with a tiny gold figure in thick mist over the lake, fading as the mist thickens and moves across the water
Close over the old chronicler hand and quill: the page fills with ink lines in a long careful script by candlelight, a century after the conquest
Freyle rides a mule up a paramo trail toward a dark lake under cloud; faint golden caiman shapes glint under the black water
Freyle bows and speaks warmly to an old Muisca priest who once kept the shrine; the priest listens, then turns to lead him up the path
The old priest reaches the edge of the dark lake and falls face down on the ground; Freyle kneels and tries to lift him, in vain
Freyle walks back down the trail empty-handed, glancing back at the small figure of the priest still lying by the far lake
A Spaniard’s gloved hand grabs for a gold piece in the glinting mud of an exposed shore
The lake whole again at dawn, one gold figurine drifting down through the dark water under the surface
A final wide view of the lake at golden dusk, mist rolling, a single thread of gold glint on the water where the raft once stood
End card: poster of the whole story with the title, the gilded heir, Freyle and the SUBSCRIBE button
